title: What Happens at the End of Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey,’ and How Does it Compare to the Real Myths?
summary: What happens at the end of The Odyssey? Does Odysseus die? What is the Telegony? Here’s how Christopher Nolan’s movie compares to mythology.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the end of “The Odyssey.”
You might have read “The Odyssey” before, but Christopher Nolan’s rendering of the epic poem, part of the Homeric cycle, offers up a brand new experience.

That’s especially true of the ending. Nolan reimagines what happens when Odysseus, played by Matt Damon, returns to Ithaca after 10 years fighting in the Trojan War and another 10 years trying to return to his kingdom.
Here’s what to know about Nolan’s twist on the ending of “The Odyssey,” how the real poem ends and the surprising, and unofficial, continuation of Odysseus’ story.
What Happens at the End of Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ — And Who Are the Sea People?
Nolan’s “Odyssey” will be unfamiliar for those who read the epic poem.

It’s a bittersweet ending for Odysseus and his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway). After murdering the suitors who had been trying to court her, Odysseus is exiled from Ithaca. He and Penelope leave their son Telemachus (Tom Holland) behind and sail west toward the setting sun, which is what Penelope dreamed they’d do when news of the Trojan War first broke out. Yes, he’s exiled — but at least they’re together.

Odysseus also reckons with the dire outlook for civilization at large and his role in it. Odysseus feels that the invasion of Troy broke “Zeus’ law,” cited throughout the movie — the code of conduct that says you should treat hosts and guests well, because anyone could be a god. The Trojan Horse, an act of war disguised as a gift, was a breach of the code.

Odysseus feels that this has led to the collapse of civilization. The “sea people,” spoken of throughout the movie with fear, are the returning Greek soldiers sacking towns, and spreading the violence that started in Troy.
He references the idea of oral history, which is how “The Odyssey” and its companion story “The Iliad” began. When people can no longer read, they will tell the stories of Troy in poems.
What Happens at the End of Homer’s ‘The Odyssey’?
“The ending of ‘The Odyssey’ is kind of strange,” Celsiana Warwick, assistant professor in the University of Iowa Department of Classics, tells TODAY.com.
The Hollywood version of the story might end with Penelope and Odysseus’ reunion. But that would have been “unsatisfying” to an ancient audience, Warwick says.

Instead, Odysseus has to face consequences for murdering all of the suitors, which compromise an elite swath of Ancient Greece’s population. The families of the suitors swarm Ithaca, wanting to get revenge on Odysseus and Telemachus. They’re about to rush into battle when the gods intervene. “Zeus hurls a thunderbolt, and Athena makes them swear a truce,” Warwick says.
Warwick adds that the ending speaks to an element of Greek culture during the archaic period “where blood feuds between aristocratic families could get way out of hand.”
“That’s something that would have been of great interest to an ancient audience, perhaps not so much to a modern audience,” she says.

Odysseus’ wandering continues, too, though his departure from Ithaca is not actually depicted in “The Odyssey.” Earlier on in the poem, the seer Tiresias tells Odysseus what he must do after killing the suitors.

In order to lift Poseidon’s curse, Odyssey has to take an oar and go on a journey until he finds men who don’t recognize it and know nothing of the sea. There, he will make a sacrifice to Poseidon, and all will be well. Tiresias predicted he would die of old age.
Jonathan Burgess, Emeritus professor of Classics, University of Toronto, calls the poem’s ending a “happy” one.

“There’s the recognition that things will follow. Poseidon’s still mad, but in the underworld, Odysseus was told how to stop Poseidon from being angry at him. There’s another adventure coming, but it’s a solution to anger from the divinity Poseidon — something you don’t want to hang over your life,” he says.
What Happens to Odysseus After ‘The Odyssey’?

“The Odyssey” ends with the gods intervening in a suitors’ battle. However, there’s more about Odysseus to be found in “other epics about the Trojan War and what happens after the Trojan War,” Burgess says.

“These existed apparently around the same time as ‘The Iliad’ and ‘The Odyssey.’ Same meter, same kind of poetry, same tradition. They told the whole story, starting from Paris and Helen to the sack of Troy,” Burgess says.
Unlike “The Iliad” and “The Odyssey,” these poems don’t exist in full. Instead, only fragments survived. Proclus, a Roman grammarian, wrote down summaries.
“The cycle poems were valued as context for Homer, but the poems themselves were not valued enough to be sung or to be preserved by the Roman period,” Burgess says.

The epic cycle concludes with “The Telegony,” which is about what happened after Odysseus’ homecoming. Author Madeline Miller looked to “The Telegony” for her popular book “Circe,” about the witch who hosts Odysseus during “The Odyssey.”
“The Telegony” is about Telegonus, the son Odysseus had during his time with Circe. Telegonus is not mentioned in “The Odyssey.”
He goes out in search of his father, carrying weapons from his mom — one being a poison-tipped spear. Eventually, he uses that spear on his father.
“Telegonus has never seen Odysseus. Odysseus has never seen Telegonus. Odysseus assumes he’s some stranger trying to steal his cattle. So they fight, and Telegonus kills his dad,” Burgess says.
Then comes something, perhaps, even stranger. First, Telegonus and Telemachus bring the corpse of Odysseus back to Aeaea, the island of Circe, and bury the body.
“Some people say Circe married Telemachus, and that Telegonus married Penelope. So there’s this strange two new weddings at the end of ‘The Telegony,’” Burgess says.

Burgess says Odysseus also remarries, according to certain myths. After leaving Ithaca to make a sacrifice for Poseidon, he travels to Epirus in northwest Greece. He married Callidice and has a son, Polypoetes, Burgess shares. After Callidice dies, he returns to Ithaca — setting the scene for “The Telegony.”
“The Telegony” place in relation to “The Odyssey” remains a mystery.
“Clearly, ‘The Telegony’ knows of ‘The Odyssey,’ but does ‘The Odyssey’ know of ‘The Telegony’”? Warwick asks.
She thinks “The Telegony” might speak to the idea of tying up loose ends.
“I think it is meant to be a happy ending. This is a way for his family to be happy without him,” Warwick says.

title: From ‘The Impossible’ to ‘Odyssey’: Watch Tom Holland’s First TODAY Interview in 2013
summary: Tom Holland made his TODAY debut in 2013 when he was 16, long before he made any “Spider-Man” movies or “The Odyssey.”
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Tom Holland’s debut on TODAY, when he chatted with Hoda Kotb and Kathie Lee Gifford on Jan. 7, 2013, while promoting his first movie, “The Impossible.”
Tom Holland has come a long way.

The actor is one of the stars of the highly anticipated summer blockbuster “The Odyssey,” alongside partner — and rumored wife —  Zendaya, Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Charlize Theron and Robert Pattinson. As if that’s not enough, Holland will also reprise the title role in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which opens July 30.
He’s gone from being a Hollywood newbie to becoming an A-lister, a transformation whose ground zero may very well have been on TODAY.

Back in 2013, when he was 16 years old, Holland stopped by to chat with Hoda Kotb and Kathie Lee Gifford in his first American TV interview while promoting his debut film, “The Impossible.” Based on a true story, the film follows a family caught in the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. It also starred Ewan McGregor and Naomi Watts, whose performance earned her an Academy Award nomination.
How Did Tom Holland Introduce Himself to Viewers?

Before he became a mega-movie star, Holland was just a teenage actor finding his footing and getting his name out there. In fact, the TODAY audience — as well as every other audience — didn’t really know him yet.
“This is my first TV show,” Holland told Hoda and Kathie Lee.
What Did Tom Holland Think About ‘The Impossible’ Making an Impact in His Life?
Kathie Lee and Hoda pointed out that Holland had been getting good reviews for “The Impossible,” which prompted Kathie Lee to ask if he was ready for how the film could change his life.

“It already has completely changed my life,” he said while noting he had been flying to Los Angeles every two weeks “to meet some of the most amazing people in the world,” although he didn’t specify who.
What Did Holland Say About Becoming Famous?
Holland had a sense that fame would soon be something he would get to understand.

“Obviously, there’s the whole thing about being recognized on the street. I’ve never had that happen before,” he said. “So that possibly will happen in the next couple of months, but I guess I’d just be polite, really.”

Getting recognized most definitely happened. Holland took over the roles of Peter Parker and Spider-Man on the big screen, first playing them in 2016’s “Captain America: Civil War” before portraying them in 2017’s “Spider-Man: Homecoming,” in addition to several more films that followed.

title: Martha Stewart Is One Proud Grandma as Truman, 14, Talks World Cup Predictions on TODAY
summary: Martha Stewart appeared on TODAY with her grandson, Truman, who spoke about his World Cup predictions as a devoted soccer fan.
story: Looks like talent runs in the family!

Truman Stewart, grandson of cooking and lifestyle maven Martha Stewart, joined TODAY on July 17 to share some of his predictions for the World Cup finals. And much like his famous grandma, Truman is a natural in front of the camera.

Truman told Steve Kornacki and the TODAY hosts that while he’s rooting for Spain, a team that many believe to be the best in the tournament, he predicts that Argentina will pull off the win on Sunday, July 19, at MetLife Stadium.
“Nothing ever really ends up how it goes based on how it looks on paper,” the 14-year-old said.
Either way, soccer fans are in for a treat, Truman said.
“The game between Spain and Argentina is just going to be one of the best I think we’ve ever seen,” Truman said.
Truman is the son of Stewart’s daughter, Alexis, who is also mom to daughter Jude. Stewart has said her two grandchildren call her simply, “Martha.”

Truman has been making predictions throughout the nearly six-week tournament with quite a bit of success. The teen correctly predicted that Spain and France would face off in the semifinals, that Argentina would appear in the finals and that Lionel Messi would carry the Argentinian team despite his age, among other clairvoyant forecasts.
While soccer is clearly his thing, Truman, who said he’s seen three World Cup games live during the tournament, admitted that he hasn’t picked up his grandma’s skills in the kitchen.
Martha Stewart, who proudly looked on during Truman’s segment, grinned as Al Roker asked her grandson, “Has she helped you make great hors d’oeuvres for the match?”
“I’ve been so focused on the games, I wouldn’t really have time for anything else,” he replied with a laugh. “And also I’m not a very good cook.”
It’s all good, Truman. Some of us were born to snack!

title: I’ve Read All 31 of Elin Hilderbrand’s Novels. Start With These 5
summary: Not sure which Elin Hilderbrand books to read next? Here are recommendations from Hilderbrand superfans to read after Five-Star Weekend.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, Elin Hilderbrand super fans recommend what to read next.
“The Five-Star Weekend” is only eight episodes, but there are many more stories from author Elin Hilderbrand to discover next.

Two of Hilderbrand’s stories have already hit the big screen through “The Five-Star Weekend” on Peacock and Netflix’s “The Perfect Couple.” (About seven more are currently in development, per the Washington Post.)
But longtime fans of the prolific author, who call themselves “Hilderbabes,” have been following along for over 25 years.

Most of Hilderbrand’s 31 novels are set in Nantucket, the Massachusetts island the author has called home for 30 years. Hilderbrand is known for writing elevated beach reads, blending heart, plot and thought-provoking premises.
The only question is: Where to start?
For this story, we spoke to Hilderbrand mega-fans:

Book influencer Katie Young, who has met and worked with Hilderbrand in person — and even got her phone number! Book influencer Samantha Brown, who discovered Hilderbrand’s books after meeting another Hilderbabe on vacation.Reader Tammy Lee Marlene, who fell back in love with reading after discovering Hilderbrand during cancer treatments. (Hilderbrand has been open about her own breast cancer diagnosis in 2014 and subsequent double mastectomy.)
Book influencer Katie Young, who has met and worked with Hilderbrand in person — and even got her phone number!
Book influencer Samantha Brown, who discovered Hilderbrand’s books after meeting another Hilderbabe on vacation.

Reader Tammy Lee Marlene, who fell back in love with reading after discovering Hilderbrand during cancer treatments. (Hilderbrand has been open about her own breast cancer diagnosis in 2014 and subsequent double mastectomy.)

Hilderbabes are committed to keeping up with the author’s work. Hilderbrand connects with her fandom in return. Every Wednesday in the summer, Hilderbrand can be found at Mitchell’s Book Corner in Nantucket, where she signs books and chats with fans.
“So much she does is for her fans, and I love that,” Young says. “I think that’s why she has this cult following. This is the book world’s Taylor Swift.”
Below, find their picks for the best introductions to Hilderbrand’s stories — and get ready for a literary escape!
‘28 Summers’ (2020)

According to the author’s super fans, “28 Summers” is frequently cited as Hilderbrand’s best book. Young compares the 2020 novel to the 1978 film “Same Time Next Year,” as it has a similar premise. In the book, two married people meet for one week each year for 28 years.
“It was so romantic and so devastating,” Brown says. “I could feel myself in the characters, and I just really didn’t want it to end. It was just so beautifully written, and I loved it.”
‘The Blue Bistro’ (2005)
“The Blue Bistro,” Hilderbrand’s fourth book, follows Adrienne Dealey, a woman who settles in Nantucket after working in hospitality for exotic resort towns.

Marlene puts “The Blue Bistro” in her top three for its ability to tell a beautiful love story without harking too much on the “will they or won’t they” of it all. The novel, which gets its name from the restaurant Adrienne stumbles into a job working at, also evokes a sensory reading experience, rich with a sense of place.

“I’m a very visual person, and her descriptions are incredible because it makes me see it,” Marlene says. “The way she’s describing the scenery, but specifically the food, she goes into such wonderful detail. It just invokes all your senses.”
‘Paradise’ and ‘Winter Street’ Series
Although most of Hilderbrand’s novels exist within the same world and feature interconnected characters, some are part of a more formal series.

Hilderbrand’s “Paradise” series (“Winter in Paradise,” “What Happens in Paradise” and “Troubles in Paradise”) is a series of thrillers set in the Caribbean island of St. John, where she spends time writing annually.
“I think (”Paradise”) grabs you in because it’s accessible. There’s drama going on. Everything’s a cliffhanger,” Young says.

Meanwhile, Hilderbrand’s “Winter Street” series (“Winter Street,” “Winter Stroll,” “Winter Storms” and “Winter Solstice”) is set on Nantucket but during the winter. The “Winter Street” series follows multiple years of family dynamics and drama within the family who owns the fictional Winter Street Inn.

“I was really invested in the characters of the Quinn family, that’s really the reason why I loved it so much, and why I love all of her books,” Brown says. “You learn so much about each character, so I really love that part of learning about family dynamics.”
‘The Hotel Nantucket’ (2022)
In this bestseller, hotel manager Lizbet Keaton tackles heartbreak by working to revive the newly renovated Hotel Nantucket, previously damaged in a fire.
Marlene ranks “The Hotel Nantucket” in her top three picks, citing Hilderbrand’s ability to build a warm and rich cadre of characters.

“You’re in the greater universe of Nantucket, but then she makes a smaller universe. ‘The Hotel Nantucket’ is about the people who work at the hotel. You have the chef and the front desk, and the guests, and there’s a ghost who gets an overview of what’s going on,” Marlene summarizes.
‘Summer of ’69’ (2019)
“Summer of ‘69” is Hilderbrand’s take on historical fiction, while still incorporating her flair for romantic drama.
“The moon landing, the Vietnam War, Ted Kennedy and Chappaquiddick island. All of that is brought up in the book. I think it’s really fun to touch on those pieces of history,” Marlene says.
Brown says she quickly became invested in the character development that deepens alongside the historical anchors.

“It’s the one I tell people to read who swear that they don’t like beach reads, because it actually reads more like a historical fiction book,” Brown says. “You fall in love. You don’t want the book to end.”

title: After ‘The Odyssey,’ Christopher Nolan Says It’ll Be ‘At Least’ 3 Years Until His Next Movie
summary: Christopher Nolan reveals how long will it be until his next movie comes out after The Odyssey’s release.
story: After anticipation building for years and showings selling out months in advance, movie fans will at last get to see Christopher Nolan’s latest epic, “The Odyssey,” on the big screen. And, it is set to be his last film for a while, he revealed.

The auteur’s newest movie, out July 17, stars Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Lupita Nyong’o, Robert Pattinson, Zendaya, Tom Holland and more A-list actors in the Homer adaptation. Bringing the Greek epic to life required elaborate sets, a massive Trojan horse and Nolan’s distinct vision.

The director and producer, who also penned the screenplay based on Homer’s work, appeared on TODAY July 17 and detailed how challenging it was to pull off the masterpiece after conceptualizing the flick for two decades.
In his sit-down with TODAY correspondent Kaylee Hartung, he explained why now was the perfect time to release the expected summer blockbuster.
“Now, I can get something made that I couldn’t otherwise get made. For me to take on Greek mythology on a big modern cinematic canvas is something that hasn’t been done,” Nolan said.
He added that the story combines many different genres.
“There’s so much in it for everybody,” he continued. “It’s a love story. It’s a coming-of-age story. It’s a story about war and homecoming. And I think that’s the eternal appeal of ‘The Odyssey.’”
Although cinephiles will have to wait a few days to see how vast that appeal is, early tracking shows “The Odyssey” could open to $200 million globally, Deadline reports.
The film is Nolan’s first since the Academy Award-winning “Oppenheimer,” which earned the director his first-ever Oscar and seven wins in total.
Fans had to wait three years for Nolan’s return with “The Odyssey.” So, when can they expect his next project?
When asked if that pattern would continue and it would be “another three years” before his next release.
He replied, “Oh, at least.”
It’s understandable given that balancing multiple genres in a nearly three-hour film was difficult for everyone involved, including Nolan.
He recalled warning Damon during one of their first conversations about “The Odyssey” that making the movie would be tough.
“I have a feeling he didn’t really understand until we got on the boat,” Nolan shared. “It’s not until you get there and you start, you know, hiking up a goat’s path to cyclops’ cave.”
He said it was at that moment that Damon had “a sort of slow creeping realization” filming was “not going to be easy.”
The Oscar-winner revealed “The Odyssey” pushed him to his limits.

“I definitely hit the limits of my own stamina and everybody’s stamina, I think. I mean, it’s ‘The Odyssey,’ of course it should be difficult,” he noted. “We’re not doing the job right making a film of ‘The Odyssey’ if it doesn’t seem difficult.”

The movie is making history as the first Hollywood production to be shot entirely on IMAX 70 millimeter film. Nolan told Hartung he needed to use the format to make the audience feel as though they were actually in a cave with a cyclops or aboard the deck of Odysseus’ ship.
Add TODAY to Google
Add TODAY to Google
He explained, “For ‘The Odyssey,’ I went to IMAX and I said, ‘Look, if ever we are going to fulfill this dream of shooting the entire movie that way, this is the one. This is ‘The Odyssey.’”
“And so for the first time ever, I finally realized that dream of doing a film that way,” added the director, who has been making movies for over 25 years.
Now that his passion project has been released, he hopes audiences flock to theaters to “experience, honestly, one of the greatest adventures” and, of course, be entertained.
He predicts they’ll have “a really phenomenal time.”

title: Who Is Elliot Page’s Character In ‘The Odyssey’? All About Sinon, Who Doesn’t Actually Appear In Homer’s Epic
summary: Does Elliot Page play Sinon or Achilles in The Odyssey? All about the character Sinon who doesn’t actually appear in the Odyssey.
story: Despite speculation that Elliot Page would be Achilles in Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” the actor isn’t playing the famous Greek warrior. In fact, Page’s character doesn’t actually appear in Homer’s “The “Odyssey” at all.

Page was cast as Sinon, a Greek warrior depicted in Virgil’s poem “The Aeneid.” Written between 29 and 19 BC. “The Aeneid” is an epic poem about about the aftermath of the Trojan War. Instead of centering on the Greeks, like “The Odyssey,” this poem follows an exiled Trojan hero, Aeneas, as he leaves Troy and lays the foundations for the future Roman Empire.
Here’s what to know about the character and how he shows up, reimagined, in Nolan’s “The Odyssey.”
Who Is Sinon?
Sinon is a key figure of Book Two of “The Aeneid,” portrayed as a master of deceit and a key part of Troy’s downfall.

After the Greeks appear to abandon the Trojan War in its final stage, Sinon remains behind, allowing himself to be captured by the Trojans. He convinces the Trojans he had been betrayed by his fellow Greek warriors.

Ultimately, he persuades the Trojans to bring the wooden horse inside the city’s walls, insisting it’s a sacred offering. Then, once the horse is inside Troy, the hidden Greek soldiers emerge, conquering the kingdom and securing its downfall.
How Does Christopher Nolan’s ‘Odyssey’ Incorporate Sinon?
Although Homer mentions the Trojan Horse in his original poem, Sinon isn’t named.
But Sinon is a huge part of Nolan’s film adaptation — in fact, the film practically opens on a close-up of his face.

The character is a key part of Odysseus’ Trojan War flashbacks. They share an even deeper bond because Odysseus selected him to go to Troy from Ithaca. Odysseus watched him grow up — and is there when he dies.
Warning: This contains spoilers for Sinon’s character.
Soona after the movie opens, Sinon is depicted standing next to the massive Trojan Horse which was constructed for the film (and came down to 36 feet and 8,000 pounds).

When approached by Trojan soldiers, Sinon swears the horse is a gift from Athena. He’s killed by the Trojans, but his guilelessness is what convinces them to bring the horse in to the city walls, paving the way for the Greeks to infiltrate. This portrayal is different than the Sinon of “The Aeneid,” who knowingly deceives the Trojans.

When Odysseus and his men visit the land of the dead in the movie, Sinon says he feels betrayed that he didn’t know the Greeks were inside the horse. Odysseus says that his complete belief was integral to the plan he devised — it was the only way the Trojans would believe him.
What Christopher Nolan and Elliot Page Said About the Role
Nolan and Page worked together previously on the 2010 sci-fi thriller “Inception,” which took home four Academy Awards.
In a recent interview, Nolan told the Rolling Stone UK that Page brought “something really special” to his performance as Sinon.

“In a way, you’re looking to put a face on certain elements of what Odysseus has done, what that means for the world as a whole. You’re looking to put a face on the tragedy of war,” Nolan said. “I think he did an incredible job.”
Page said getting to have a “Chris Nolan experience” after coming out as trans “meant so much,” he told a New York City Comic Con panel in 2025, per Variety.
“Being more comfortable in yourself makes these sorts of projects more enjoyable,” he added.

title: Kris Jenner Announces Death of Mother Mary Jo ‘MJ’ Shannon at 91. Read the Emotional Statement
summary: Mary Jo “MJ” Shannon, the mother of Kardashian “momager” Kris Jenner, has died, Jenner announced on July 16. Read what she read
story: Mary Jo “MJ” Shannon, the mother of Kardashian “momager” Kris Jenner, has died, Jenner announced on July 16. She was 91 years old.
Jenner shared a heartfelt post about her mother, describing her as the “heart of our family.”

“Today, we said goodbye to my beautiful Mommy MJ,” Jenner said of Shannon in her social media post. “There are no words that could ever capture what she has meant to me or the heartbreak of having to say goodbye.”

In her social media post, Jenner reflected on the ways in which Shannon, known to fans of “The Kardashians” as “MJ,” had impacted her throughout the course her life. Shannon was the grandmother to the family’s famous stars including Kim Kardashian, Kourtney Kardashian, Kendall Jenner and Kylie Jenner.

“She taught me everything that truly matters… to love your family fiercely, to be kind, to show up for the people you love, and to never take a single moment together for granted,” Jenner wrote. “She taught us that family is everything. She showed us how to love unconditionally and how to find joy in the little moments. She showed me how to face life’s challenges with resilience and faith.”
Jenner, who said she was grateful for “every sacrifice” her mother made, also shared the aspects of Shannon that she will grieve.

“I will miss our daily talks, your smile, your laughter… Our hearts are broken, but we find comfort knowing that love like yours never truly leaves us,” Jenner wrote. “Your love will live on in our family, in our traditions, in every moment we are together, and in every life you touched.”
While Jenner said that the loss will be difficult for her and the family, she added that Shannon’s memory will live on.

“When I look at my kids and my grandkids, I will forever see pieces of you in all of us. There is not a part of me that isn’t shaped by you. And if I have done anything right in this world, it’s because I spent my life trying to live in a way that would make you proud,” Jenner wrote. “Every memory, every moment, every blessing, it was all because of you, and I will forever thank God every single day for making you my mommy.”
Jenner concluded her post by thanking Shannon for “giving us everything.”
“My heart is broken into a million pieces… thank you for giving me the greatest childhood and oh what a beautiful blessed life…” Jenner wrote. “I love you forever Mommy.”

Several other members of the Kardashian family also shared emotional messages about Shannon. Kim Kardashian described her late grandmother in an Instagram post as her “best friend, my gossip buddy, my forever twin.”
“You taught all of us the importance of family, and those values are something we’ll carry with us forever!!!!!” Kardashian wrote on social media.

Kardashian added that Shannon was the one who taught her “what it meant to be a hardworking businesswoman.” She explained in the post that her grandmother had given her her first job at a store Shannon owned in San Diego.

“You always believed in me, championed me, and were my safe place. You truly were the matriarch of our family, and your love is woven into all of us,” Kardashian wrote, calling on Shannon to embrace several of her late family members including her father Robert Kardashian, who died in 2003. “I know you’re at peace now.”
Kourtney Kardashian Barker also posted a sweet photo of Shannon on her Instagram stories while Khloe Kardashian shared a tearful moment between Jenner and Shannon from the family’s reality show.

In the past, Jenner has opened up about how Shannon’s health. During a 2025 episode of “The Kardashians,” Jenner broke down when reflecting on her mother’s well-being after Karen Houghton, Shannon’s younger daughter, died unexpectedly in 2024.
“Ever since my sister passed away, she’s been super sad, like we all have, and I know that I need to be there for her,” Jenner said.
In the episode, Shannon revealed she hadn’t been to her kitchen for two days due to pain she had been experiencing.
“This makes me really sad,” an emotional Jenner said in the episode. “I just hate it when she’s in so much pain.”

title: Matt Damon and His ‘Odyssey’ Co-Stars Debate What the Film Is Really About
summary: Matt Damon and the co stars of “The Odyssey” unpack what the tale is really about, what they did in preparation for the film and weigh in on Damon’s ultimate sacrifice.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Christopher Nolan’s three-hour opus “The Odyssey” lands in theaters today. With tickets selling out more than a year (yes, a year) in advance, the epic film is one of the most anticipated cinematic events of 2026, if not the decade.

At the helm is Matt Damon, who said on TODAY his “whole professional life built up to this experience.” Starring as Odysseus, he plays a Greek king leading his people home after the bloody Trojan War, driven by a personal goal of reaching his wife and son. As No. 1 on the call sheet, his co-stars say Damon was as much a leader off screen as he was on.

Filmed over six months in an equal number locations around the world, “The Odyssey” boasts a certified A-list lineup: Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland as Odysseus’ wife and son, Penelope and Telemachus; Zendaya as Athena; Charlize Theron as Calypso; Himesh Patel as Odysseus’ second in command; Robert Pattinson and Corey Hawkins as Antinous and Polybus, suitors of Penelope; the list goes on.

Ahead of the premiere, cast members stopped by Studio 1A to share their thoughts on Nolan’s most ambitious project to date. Below, Damon, Patel and Hawkins chat with TODAY.com to talk Greek mythology, commiserate over going gluten-free and fangirl over Patel’s turn in the 2019 Beatles movie “Yesterday.”

title: Keyne, Baby Brother of Spanish Soccer Star Lamine Yamal, Is Stealing the World Cup Spotlight
summary: The 3-year-old brother of Spanish phenom Lamine Yamal has captured the internet’s attention during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
story: On the pitch, young phenom Lamine Yamal has been delighting soccer fans as he looks to secure the 2026 FIFA World Cup victory for Spain. But in the stands, it’s his adorable 3-year-old brother Keyne who has been keeping viewers entertained.

Yamal, 19, and his teammates are headed to the World Cup finals game against Argentina on July 19. Spain has overcome multiple difficult opponents, including France in their semifinal matchup. And Yamal’s younger brother could be their good luck charm.

Throughout the tournament, Keyne — Yamal’s half-brother who shares their mother Sheila Ebana — has been charming viewers with his excitement for his big brother and adorable fan interactions. Social media users just can’t get enough.

One fan shared an adorable video on X, featuring an excited Keyne, passionately shouting “vamos” when Spain defeated Austria 3-1 in the round of 32 on July 2. The video received more than 32,000 likes.
Yamal, who was named the player of the match, opened up about his relationship with his brother after the intense game.
“I’m moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of,” he said, according to The New York Times’ The Athletic.
He sweetly added: “My little brother means everything to me. I am in love with him; it feels like he is my son.”

In another viral moment, during Spain’s match against Belgium in the quarterfinals on July 10, an enthused Keyne was caught on camera, making silly faces and sticking out his tongue. Yamal appeared to laugh after catching a glimpse of his baby brother on the Jumbotron. That moment similarly got a lot of love from fans, drawing upwards of 38,000 likes in one social media post.
And another cute picture of Keyne waving to Yamal after Spain’s 2-0 win over France on July 14, shared by ESPN’s SportsCenter, went viral as well.

Following that match, Yamal shared a carousel on Instagram to celebrate. The final snap showed the soccer star, sitting with Keyne and Ebana in the stands. In the photo, Yamal is staring at his baby bro.
Throughout the tournament, Ebana has been giving fans a glimpse into the adventures that she’s been having with Keyne as they travel the U.S. amid the contest.

On July 5, she shared videos on Instagram of their day at the Santa Monica Pier and Venice Beach in Los Angeles. Ebana also posted videos days later of the family’s visit to the Hollywood Walk of Fame, where Keyne encountered a Freddy Krueger impersonator. In the clip, the brave 3-year-old appears to be more excited than scared. Because he’s a legend.
As shown in social media posts, Ebana and Keyne also hiked to LA’s iconic Hollywood Sign and visited the Griffith Observatory.

More photos of Keyne’s adventures were shared when Yamal celebrated his 19th birthday on July 13. Proud mom Ebana uploaded snaps that Keyne, holding some gold-colored “19” balloons. In another snap, Keyne stares up at Yamal, who’s looks like he’s about to blow out the candles on his two birthday cakes. One of the final photos in Ebana’s photo carousel showed the family, heading to a match while sporting Yamal’s jersey.

title: Chloe Fineman Leaving ‘SNL’ After 7 Seasons: ‘Greatest Privilege of My Life’
summary: Chloe Fineman revealed that she is leaving “Saturday Night Live” after being on the show for seven seasons.
story: After seven seasons of viral sketches and celebrity impressions, Chloe Fineman is leaving “Saturday Night Live” ahead of its 52nd season.
The comedian announced on Instagram July 16 that she is departing from the show, describing her time on the comedy staple as “the greatest privilege” of her life.

“It’s really hard to leave SNL but it does feel like the right time,” Fineman wrote. “I’m going to miss it a lot. But the people who work there are my family and that place is my home, and I know I’ll never be too far away.”

Her departure follows a slew of exits from many of the show’s veteran comedians in 2025, including Heidi Gardner, Ego Nwodim and Bowen Yang, as well as Michael Longfellow, Devon Walker and Emil Wakim, who were shorter-tenured performers.
Ahead of the Season 51 premiere in September 2025, Fineman told Extra TV that she was still wrapping her head around the shakeups.
“Some shocking stuff,” she said. “A little heartbreak, sadness. I haven’t fully processed anything, but I will say the show has such a turnover.”

In the post announcing her departure, Fineman wrote about the highs and lows of working on the show: “I still can’t really believe I got to be a part of it. I fell in love with the place the second I walked through the door.”

She also joked about the plights of working on “SNL,” recalling how performers can “sob uncontrollably” when a sketch is cut, only to look back “a few years later” and realize “it was a sketch called ‘lipstick for thicc dogs.’”
Fineman wrapped up her farewell message with a final declaration about the sketch: “And I swear to God, one day, sometime in the future, they WILL make lipstick for thicc dogs,” she wrote.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Reacts to Will Ferrell’s Impression of Her Dad: ‘I Was Hoping This Was Coming!’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager laughed when Will Ferrell did his impression of her father, former President George W. Bush, on TODAY.
story: Jenna Bush Hager still can’t get enough of Will Ferrell’s impression of her father, former President George W. Bush.

Much to her delight, the funnyman broke out his classic impression of her dad when he stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on July 16, along with Molly Shannon, Luke Wilson, Fortune Feimster and Jimmy Tatro, his costars from Netflix’s new golf comedy “The Hawk.” The group played a game of “Putt or Dare,” where they had to perform a challenge if they missed a short putt.

Ferrell was tasked with doing three celebrity impressions after he came up just short on his shot. First, he spoke as of Ron Burgundy, his beloved character from the “Anchorman” movies. Then he resurfaced his well-known take on late baseball broadcaster Harry Caray.
He then launched into his final impression: Jenna’s father, George W. Bush, whom he often portrayed during his time on “Saturday Night Live.”
“Here’s the thing about golf ...” he began.
“I was hoping this was coming!” Jenna said.
Ferrell then looked at Jenna as he continued.
“We used to talk about this when you were just a little girl,” he said while everyone, including Jenna, laughed.
“You need a lot of strategery to get the ball in the hole,” he continued, as he fought off laughter.
“That’s your dad,” Ferrell, who turned 59 on July 16, said, finally breaking character while everyone applauded.

Ferrell made the word “strategery” famous during a 2000 “Saturday Night Live” sketch in which Ferrell’s Bush squared off against Darrell Hammond’s Al Gore in a presidential debate. Contrary to popular belief, Bush never used the word “strategery.” It was created by longtime “Saturday Night Live” writer Jim Downey.
Ferrell has busted out the impression on TODAY before.
“Here’s a funny story: I didn’t realize that I never said ‘strategery,’” he said in a Bush voice during a 2022 appearance with Hoda Kotb and Jenna. “Someone else wrote that.”
Jenna confirmed that her father never actually said the word. Despite that, she said her dad never had a problem with Ferrell — or anyone else — parodying him.

“I like to harass my dad,” Jenna said in 2024 on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna. “When he was the president, Barbara and I would show him the ‘Saturday Night Live’s’ where they made fun of him and stuff. He loved it.”
She also said her dad understood that getting lampooned came with the job.

“If you’re going to be the president of the United States, people are going to make fun of you,” she said. “And guess what, it ain’t just about you. That’s how it is, man. That’s how it’s always been.”

title: TSA Has Thoughts After Erling Haaland Seen Carrying a Taxidermy Raccoon Off a Plane
summary: Norway striker Erling Haaland was photographed holding a taxidermy raccoon holding an empty liquor bottle. TSA responded.
story: Norway’s striker Erling Haaland spent his summer in the United States playing in the World Cup, and returned home with a unique souvenir.
The 25-year-old soccer star made headlines when he was photographed carrying a taxidermy raccoon holding an empty liquor bottle when getting off a plane at Oslo’s Gardermoen Airport on July 13.
Sharing a photo from his arrival to his X account, Haaland quipped, “It followed me home.”
As the photos of him and his gift went viral, it caught the attention of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), who shared some thoughts on what people can and can’t fly with.
“We’re getting some questions about flying with taxidermy raccoons holding empty liquor bottles,” reads TSA’s July 14 message on social media. “It’s ok with us but pls check with your airline first.”

The taxidermy raccoon was purchased during his visit to Wild Bill’s Western Store in Dallas, according to the local store. On their Instagram story, they shared Haaland’s photo and commented, “We know that raccoon! so cool seeing our little raccoon made it to Norway.”
Haaland filmed his visit to the store and shared the experience in a July 3 YouTube video he titled “Norway’s Texas Takeover.”

The 10-minute vlog shows the athlete trying on a variety of western wear, including boots and hats. It appears that he purchased “four hats, three winter hats and one summer” hat, according to the salesman in the video.
While shopping around, Haaland also expressed interest in a shirt that said, “Y’all can kiss my Dallas.”
Haaland, who became an online sensation for U.S. World Cup viewers, couldn’t believe how welcoming everyone was.
“Unbelievable, so nice. I’m coming back here,” he said. “People are so nice here. So positive. Don’t know what it is, they’re... enjoying life. It’s amazing.”
Haaland and the rest of Team Norway were unfortunately eliminated during the quarterfinals. They returned to their home country after they lost to England on July 11.
Since Haaland’s visit, sales from Wild Bill’s have skyrocketed. The store has even begun to offer international shipping for the first time in its history, owner Julie Newport told The Athletic.

“We are somewhere around 2,000 online orders right now, about 30 per cent of that is international but every day when we wake up, we have more orders,” Newport told the outlet. “For international, we just didn’t have that ability turned on before (Haaland visited).”
While Haaland didn’t share footage of his raccoon purchase, which retails for $750, the store still experienced significant interest in its taxidermy selection.

“We’ve had a couple of these taxidermy raccoons in the store for the last few years, and he obviously gravitated to that and a couple of the squirrels,” Newport told The Athletic. “(Since he posted on social media), we ordered another raccoon — we put it out on the floor today but by the time we put it on the floor, someone already bought it online.”
Unfortunately, the taxidermy specialist from whom the store purchased its critters has retired, so there is limited stock of the famous raccoon, Newport told the outlet.
The store isn’t shy about its association to Haaland. Its website proudly displays a blurb about its famous fan.

“Looking for one of the most talked-about souvenirs at Wild Bill’s?” the website says. “Our squirrels and raccoons gained worldwide attention after soccer superstar Erling Haaland shared photos from his visit to Wild Bill’s Western Store during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, introducing millions of fans to one of Texas’ most unexpected western traditions.”

title: Anne Hathaway Tears up At TODAY’s ‘Odyssey’-Themed Baby Gift: ‘Appropriately Epic’
summary: Anne Hathaway, currently pregnant with her third child, received a crochet baby outfit inspired by the “Odyssey” during her interview with Tom Holland on TODAY.
story: Homer’s epic poem warns that accepting a gift can be a dangerous decision. But “The Odyssey” star Anne Hathaway was seemingly moved to tears by TODAY’s present for her baby-on-the-way.

During an interview July 16 alongside her onscreen son Tom Holland, Craig Melvin surprised Hathaway with a custom “Odyssey”-inspired crochet baby outfit. The ensemble, resembling battle armor, included a diaper cover, a cape and a helmet.
“When the child comes out, we want the child ready for battle,” Craig joked.
Hathaway appeared particularly excited about the cape included with the outfit.
“This is appropriately epic, thank you so much,” she said.
Holland was equally impressed by the crochet handiwork.
“Tom, when you have your child,” Craig said, before Holland added, “I know where to come. I’ll come right back here.”
Hathaway, 43, announced her pregnancy with baby No. 3 via Instagram in June. She and her husband Adam Shulman, who married in 2012, are already parents to sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6.
“x Baby, I’m yours x,” Hathaway captioned the clip of her showing off her baby bump for the first time, set to the tune of Barbara Lewis’ “Baby, I’m Yours.”
Prior to giving Hathaway her gift, Craig read a social media post praising the actor for balancing her packed slate of projects with her growing family.
“Anne Hathaway having 5 movies premiering this year and then announcing that she’s pregnant is the level of productivity that men can’t achieve,” the post on X read.
“I mean (men) are at a disadvantage,” Hathaway replied through laughter. “It’s just a literal truth.”
“It’s amazing,” Craig said, “You’ve made everyone else in Hollywood look and feel lazy.”
Hathaway said throughout her career she’s experienced peaks, valleys and “everything in between.”
“It’s just crazy to have a time like this where you pull these cards, and the thing that’s so exciting is they’re films that audiences want to see,” she said.

“To be a part of something, a part of year where so many people are just excited to go out, experience cinema,” she added. “And then yeah, to have this personal thing going on at the same time. It’s amazing.”
In the spring, Hathaway rolled out “Mother Mary” and “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” Now, she’s gearing up for the premieres of “The Odyssey,” “The End of Oak Street” and “Verity.”
“The Odyssey” hits theaters July 17.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Reviews: What Critics Said to Earn the Movie a 98% Rotten Tomatoes Score
summary: Here is what the critics are saying about Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” which stars Matt Damon, Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland.
story: It looks like Christopher Nolan may have hit a Homer-run with the “The Odyssey.” The 172-minute blockbuster, written and directed by the “Oppenheimer” Academy Award winner, is poised to be one of the films of the summer, and the reviews may back up all the hype.

The long-awaited movie, starring Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Charlize Theron, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Samantha Morton, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Elliot Page and Jon Bernthal hits theaters July 17.
“The Odyssey” is an adaptation of Homer’s classic poem, revolving around the Greek king Odysseus (played by Damon), who endures a long and daunting journey home after the Trojan War.
The early reaction to the film was favorable, but now the reviews are in, and it looks like the film may very well live up to the hoopla, earning a decadent 98% score on Rotten Tomatoes.
Here’s a look at what the critics are saying about “The Odyssey.”
Variety
Guy Lodge lauded the scope and ambition of the movie.

“A genuinely grand, gutsy vision, “The Odyssey” thrills generously for the bulk of its near three-hour running time: Every few minutes, it seems, it throws at its audience another mighty set piece that, in almost any other summer studio spectacle, would be a climactic standout,” he wrote in his review for Variety.
Lodge liked the “inspired casting of Matt Damon” and the other casting decisions.

“The Odyssey” is a veritable banquet, then, of such loud, grandiose, movie-movie pleasures, so brashly, confidently lavish that it can afford to throw away a significant portion of its all-star cast on lily-gilding cameos,” he wrote.

“There’s so much to feel here at a sensory level that the film gets away with its slightly aloof, soul-skirting chill; we leave it feeling that we’ve been to hell and back, and exhilaratingly so,” he added.
Rolling Stone
“Nolan and his behind-the-camera collaborators want to wow you,” wrote David Fear, who ultimately concludes that’s exactly what he does.

“What you tend to walk away with after bearing witness to ‘The Odyssey,’ arguably Christopher Nolan’s best work after 2017’s ‘Dunkirk,’ is an overall sensation of awe,” he wrote in wrapping up his review.

“It is one of the most dynamic movies in recent memory, simply in the way it attempts to — and largely succeeds — balance such incredible highs and delicate lows, deafening bursts of divine wrath with quiet pauses of contemplation, episodic moments of old-school Saturday-matinee fantasy with the sort of grounded interactions associated with smaller projects.

“A cynical wiseass might, sight unseen, crack that it took one of the greatest epic tales ever told to finally find material that matched Nolan’s ambitions. Once you’ve stepped into this film and let it sweep you up, however, it’s hard to deny the accomplishment that he’s brought to the screen. You may have no idea how long you’ve been gone after you’ve seen it. You just know that you want to go back again.”
The Hollywood Reporter
For The Hollywood Reporter, David Rooney did call the movie “uneven,” but singled out many of the film’s performances.

“Damon is superb, going to dark places seldom if ever explored in his previous roles; Hathaway is a model of steely self-possession masking vulnerability; Pattinson bites into his character’s villainy with gusto, showing Antinous to be a cowardly conspirator, loyal only to himself,” he wrote.
He also lauded the action sequences.
“The push for in-camera spectacle over digital fakery wherever possible pays off in terms of dropping the audience right into the middle of the action,” he wrote.
Associated Press
Jake Coyle wrote for the Associated Press that Damon took on “the role of his life” in this “richly textured film.”
“While ‘The Odyssey,’ Nolan’s first film shot entirely with IMAX cameras, doesn’t skimp on grandiosity, it works surprisingly well as a simpler, human-sized tale,” he wrote.
Coyle also said the movie will take its place in the Nolan canon.

“But ‘The Odyssey’ is rarely not transfixing, and it’s a ripping adventure story, besides. At the least, it’s the definitive big-screen adaptation of one of literature’s oldest tales — a not-too-shabby accomplishment for a filmmaker of restless ambition,” he wrote.
Forbes
“‘The Odyssey’ is a visual masterpiece filled with grand production and set designs, detailed costumes, and the most unsettling action sequences,” Laura Sirikul wrote.

“The war and fight sequences, particularly in the final act, are a masterclass in storytelling, direction, sound, music, set design and action. All of which feels grand in scale and heart-pounding, as if we were there,” she continued.
She wrapped up her take on the film by praising it as a classic.
“It’s a tale that only Nolan could have really told with this massive Hollywood production — and he did it epically,” she wrote.
The New York Times
Manohla Dargis was in awe of Nolan’s work, pointing out how it effortlessly slides into his catalog of pictures.

“Nolan’s love of movies and commitment to them — to what they can do, what they can be, what they should be — runs like an electric current through his filmography, lighting it, and oftentimes you, up,” she wrote.

“That passion is in every frame of his monumental adaptation of ‘The Odyssey,’ one of the most Nolan of Nolan spectacles in its thematic concerns, formal playfulness, kinetic thrills and unabashed showmanship.”
“Nolan’s gifts are excessively obvious, and even when his characters don’t stir you, his filmmaking does,” she continued.

“Among other qualities, he doesn’t know how to make an ugly image and this one is filled with rapturous beauty. Nolan employs beauty strategically, using it to seduce viewers into stories that can seem needlessly byzantine to some — especially by impoverished mainstream industry standards — more the provenance of the art house than the multiplex. Nolan asks us to dream bigger. His ‘Odyssey’ is a classic in every sense, a transporting affirmation of the art and a work of pure cinema.”
Mashable
Belen Edwards bowed down at the foot of Nolan’s work, citing his efforts into a new genre.
“So, how does Nolan approach his first foray into epic fantasy? How does he fare when turning his lens to antiquity and one of its foundational myths?” Edwards wrote.

“The answer, in a word, is spectacularly. Nolan eschews the sleek modernity that’s come to define his filmography. Instead, he gives himself up to a grimy, haunting take on ‘The Odyssey’ that weaves myth and history into a devastating, unforgettable reckoning for Odysseus himself.”
Edwards also saluted Nolan’s ability to work on a grand scale, while also maintaining a personal touch.

“‘The Odyssey’s’ magnificent conclusion would not work if Nolan didn’t hold audiences close to the action every step of the way. Yes, the film is a glorious spectacle, boasting vast ocean vistas, armies of giants, and even the occasional sea monster. But Nolan doesn’t just want ‘The Odyssey’ to be epic. He wants it to be human, too.”
NME

“The word ‘epic’ has been tossed around a lot over the last 3,000 years… Leave it to Christopher Nolan, then, to remind us what a proper epic looks, sounds and feels like,” Paul Bradshaw began his five-star review. If ‘Oppenheimer’ was a small story made big, ‘The Odyssey’ is a big story made impossibly huge: delivering yet another landmark summer cinema event that might just be the director’s most accomplished film to date.”
Bradshaw also marveled at Nolan’s ability to make sense of a complex story.
“Always a master of structure, Nolan’s real coup here is cutting the poem up into bits and piecing it all back together again,” he wrote.

“Less a case of them not making ‘em like they used to, watching the film leaves you with a sense that this sort of thing probably won’t be made at all for too much longer — the sheer scale, ambition and weight of it seeming to belong to a different world already,” he added. “It’s hard to see how cinema can get much bigger than this.”

title: Jennifer Garner Hosted Her Own ‘Five-Star Weekend’: ‘I Kind of Threw Myself a Wedding’
summary: Jen Garner and Elin Hilderbrand joined Jenna Bush Hager on her podcast Open Book With Jenna on an episode that aired on July 16.
story: In Elin Hilderbrand’s bestselling novel “The Five-Star Weekend,” food influencer Hollis Shaw, reeling from the sudden death of her husband, invites four friends from four different stages of life to a weekend away in Nantucket, Massachusetts.
What begins as a heartfelt attempt to reconnect quickly unravels as long-buried secrets come to the surface, old wounds are reopened and the women confront major life decisions.
Jennifer Garner, who stars as Hollis in Peacock’s adaptation of the novel, said she’s experienced her own version of a “Five-Star Weekend” in real life.

Speaking with Jenna on the July 16 episode of her “Open Book with Jenna” podcast, where Hilderbrand also appeared as a guest, Garner reflected on her latest “Five-Star”-adjacent extravaganza: Gathering friends from every chapter of her life for her 50th birthday on April 17, 2022.
“I just had friends from my whole life. I kind of threw myself a wedding,” said Garner, now 54.

The milestone birthday happened to fall on Easter for the first time in her life, she said, granting her an extra-long celebration. More importantly, it gave the actor an opportunity to bring people together who rarely crossed over.

“One night it was just the girls, and it was so special and fun because I also have this little posse of works friends that I shoot with, like the people I’ve been with forever since ‘Alias,’ and they were part of it as well,” she explained.
“Usually it’s like when I’m with when I’m working, I live that life, and otherwise I just see them now and then. So to have everybody together was especially special.”

The jam-packed weekend also featured a memorable surprise from Garner’s teen crush, Donny Osmond, TODAY.com previously reported. The singer appeared with a custom cake that read: “13 going on 50! Love Donny!”
Hilderbrand, on the other hand, told Jenna that she has never quite embraced the premise of her own novel.

“For the last 33 years, (Nantucket) has been my world. So almost all of my friends are friends that I’ve met on Nantucket,” the author said. “I have my girlfriends from college and I have friends from high school, but the two worlds have not collapsed.”
“You’ve got to make it happen,” Jenna insisted.
“It would be so weird,” Hilderbrand replied, in part. “Like, would it work?”
Garner chimed in: “Yes, it would work. It’s worked for me. It’ll work for you. Women, we look for ways to connect.”

title: Savannah Guthrie Shares She’s Off to Film Wordle Game Show for a Couple of Weeks
summary: Savannah Guthrie shared on TODAY Thursday that she will be away from the show for a few weeks to film a new Wordle game show she is hosting.
story: Savannah Guthrie shared on TODAY Thursday that she will be away from the show for a few weeks to film a new Wordle game show she is hosting.
“I’m headed over to shoot ‘Wordle’ over the next few weeks,” Savnnah said on TODAY July 16. “We’re going to shoot the whole season, and we’re super excited. Cannot wait for everyone to see it.”

Savannah had previously announced on TODAY in May that she would be hosting the new NBC show, which is based on the popular online puzzle game in which you try to guess a five-letter word in six tries or less.
“The Tonight Show” host Jimmy Fallon is executive producing the new show alongside The New York Times, which owns Wordle.

“We were looking, we’re like, ‘Who’s the perfect host for this? We need to have someone that looks like they play Wordle, someone that knows how to run a show and host it.’ And we did the pilot, and you are amazing,” Fallon said about Savannah on TODAY in May.

Teams of three avid Wordle players will go head-to-head in solving puzzles on the show for a cash prize. Fallon said the show has been in development for two-plus years. Wordle made its debut in 2021 and became a pandemic obsession for millions of players. The New York Times purchased the game in 2022 and offers Wordle for free in the New York Times Games app on iOS and Android, as well as mobile web and desktop.
The game show is expected to premiere in 2027 and will air in primetime.

TODAY and The New York Times also announced in an exclusive on July 16 that fans can solve TODAY-themed Wordle puzzles for a chance to win VIP access to Citi Concert Series performances this summer by artists like Tyla, Shaboozey, Bebe Rexha and more.
